newsitem.title: CHINA: S.Africa to retain HK consulate after handover.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to retain HK consulate after handover.

text.p: South Africa, which is to switch diplomatic recognition to China from Taiwan at the end of 1997, will keep its consulate in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Beijing on July 1, officials said on Thursday.

"The successful cooperation in regard to Hong Kong represents an important breakthrough," South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said in a statement after talks in Beijing with Chinese officials.

"(This) signifies a strong commitment by both the Republic of South Africa and the People's Republic of China toward a constructive approach in finding solutions to mutual problems through negotiations," he said.

In his second round of talks with Chinese officials in Beijing on Monday, Pahad had reached agreement allowing South Africa to retain its consulate-general in Hong Kong from July 1 until Beijing and Pretoria formalise ties on January 1, 1998, the statement said.

Failure to reach agreement before Beijing resumes sovereignty over the British colony at midnight on June 30 would have forced South Africa to downgrade the consulate to the status of a non-governmental organisation.
The two sides agreed to continue the current practice of exempting Hong Kong and South African travellers from requiring visas, the statement said.
The two sides agreed that South Africa would maintain existing air services with Hong Kong and Beijing agreed to grant South African Airways overflight rights to Japan.
Trade between Hong Kong and South Africa in 1996 totalled $1.5 billion and investment in South Africa was more than $270 million, the statement said.
Pahad left Beijing for Hong Kong on Wednesday.
